content: Stanford Natural Language Inference (SNLI) dataset BIBREF30 consist of 570,000 pairs of sentences. Each pair has a premise and a hypothesis, manually labeled with one of the three labels: entailment, contradiction, or neutral. The SNLI has many desired properties. The labels are equally balanced, as opposed to the RCV1 dataset. Additionally, language inference is a complex task that requires a deeper understanding of the sentence meaning making this dataset suitable for learning supervised sentence encoders that generalize well to other tasks BIBREF17 . tbl:snliexmaples, shows examples of SNLI dataset sentence pairs and its respective labels.
